title: Trace session playback and snapshotting - grooming notes
content:
Purpose:

Quick grooming doc to capture design decisions, interaction notes, and backlog items for a new Trace Viewer feature: session playback + trace snapshotting. Aim: let engineers and SREs capture a moment-in-time trace, play it back (time-scrub and step-through spans), and share or compare snapshots across time or releases. This is intended as a production-first UX pattern (fast, low cognitive load) that integrates with rollouts and alerting flows.

Background / motivation:
- Currently we have a static waterfall + span inspector. Users want an ability to:
  * capture a reproducible trace view (pins filters, time window, model/route context) for later review or handoff,
  * play traces as a timeline (scrub forward/back, play at 0.5x/1x/2x),
  * step through span lifecycles and see associated logs/metrics aligned in time,
  * compare two snapshots side-by-side to validate regression fixes or config changes.
- Common asks surfaced in support threads and SE handoffs: INF-1123, linear thread #trace-help.

Design goals / constraints:
- Lightweight: snapshot should be a small, shareable object (no 1:1 raw trace storage duplication).
- Reproducible: snapshot captures query params + filters + model/route/version + prefetched relevant logs/annotations.
- Fast discovery: new "Snapshots" panel accessible from trace header; quick keyboard shortcut ("s") to create snapshot.
- Security: maintain access controls (snapshots respect the same org/route RBAC), ephemeral token URLs only when user opts to share externally.
- Storage: tier snapshots (ephemeral 7d by default, persistent on explicit save).

User journeys (happy paths):
1) Developer investigating a 500:
   - Open trace > notice anomaly > press `S` or click "Capture snapshot" > modal: name + reason + attach active logs checkbox.
   - Snapshot saved; system generates short share link and attaches to current incident in SRE channel.
   - Recipient opens snapshot; UI reconstructs filters + places playhead at anomaly span.
2) SRE regression comparison:
   - Search snapshots by tag (eg. release-2025-11-01) > select two snapshots > click "Compare" > UI shows synchronized waterfalls with playhead sync; toggles for overlay vs side-by-side.
3) Postmortem authoring:
   - From incident timeline, drag snapshot into postmortem draft (auto-inserts link + small inline image preview).

Wireframe / interaction notes (text sketches):
- Trace header: Add "Snapshots" button next to "Share". Clicking opens a bottom-sheet panel listing recent snapshots (filterable).
- Create snapshot modal: fields: Title, Tags (freeform), TTL (7d / 30d / permanent), Include logs (checkbox), Attach to incident (dropdown). Primary CTA: "Capture snapshot". Secondary: "Capture + open playback".
- Playback bar (new small control above waterfall):
  * Play/Pause, step-backward, step-forward, speed selector (0.5x/1x/2x), loop toggle, current timestamp.
  * Scrubber shows small thumbnail of active spans as you hover (sparklines).
- Snapshot lane: a thin horizontal lane above waterfall with markers for saved snapshots. Hover shows tooltip (title, created-by, short note). Click opens snapshot in isolated mode (left panel collapsed).
- Isolated snapshot mode: UI reconstructs filters and opens compact playback-first layout: waterfall center, inspector on right minimized, timeline controls prominent. Top bar shows snapshot metadata and share actions.
- Compare mode: split view with synchronized scrubbing by default. Optional color-coding of spans that differ in duration or status. Show percent delta for overall request latency and top N affected spans.

Playback semantics / alignment rules:
- Playhead moves in real time according to timeline; when hitting a span start, inspector flashes/highlights span.
- For multi-span services (eg. fan-out), default play visualization: nested expansion opens automatically on first play unless user toggles collapsed preference.
- Logs/metrics alignment: when logs are attached, the logs strip scrolls with playhead and auto-filter to events within +/- 250ms window.

Snapshot storage and footprint:
- Snapshot stores: query string + filters, trimmed list of top-level spans (+span ids) and a small window of serialized annotations/logs for those spans (limit 10KB per span default).
- If user chooses persistent storage, snapshot size cap 1MB; otherwise ephemeral snapshots purged after TTL.
- Link generation: opaque short id (e.g. /snap/abc123). External share produces time-limited token (30d or custom).

Backlog / grooming items (rough):
- INF-2147: Snapshot capture flow + modal (3 SP) - priority: P0 for cycle 1.
- INF-2151: Playback controls + scrubber thumbnails (5 SP) - priority: P0.
- INF-2163: Compare mode + delta metrics (8 SP) - priority: P1.
- INF-2170: Storage + TTL policies + RBAC checks (5 SP) - priority: P0.
- INF-2175: UI accessibility pass (keyboard focus, ARIA labels) (2 SP) - priority: P1.
- INF-2180: Attach snapshot to incident & postmortem integration (3 SP) - priority: P1.
- Spike: Feasibility for compact serialized logs vs pointer to raw log store (1 SP) - assign to eng-applied-ml for cost estimate.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP snapshot + playback):
- User can capture a snapshot from any trace and reopen it reconstructing filters + playhead position.
- Playback controls are responsive with <100ms UI latency for scrubbing on sample 50k token traces.
- Snapshot share link opens the same UI state for other org users (respecting RBAC).
- Storage TTL enforced and visible on snapshot listing.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should snapshots store raw span payloads or only references (risk: raw payload keeps historical view but costs more)? Proposed: hybrid - default reference + cached minimal payload; allow permanent snapshot option that stores full payload.
- How to handle changing model/route versions: snapshot should record version string and display "served_by: v12 (current v14)" with warning if version drift exists.
- Compare UI: overlay vs side-by-side — which is easier for quick diffs? Initial MVP: side-by-side with synchronized playhead + delta badges.
- Offline consumption: can snapshots be exported as a JSON artifact for embedding in postmortems? Yes — expose download button (small export).

Accessibility notes:
- All playback actions must be keyboard operable: space toggles play/pause; left/right arrows step; shift+arrows seek 10s.
- Provide non-visual summary export (text timeline + key spans) for screen readers.

Edge cases and anti-patterns:
- Very large traces: when captured, provide warning and suggest trimmed snapshot (top-N spans by duration) or auto-sampling.
- Sensitive PII in logs: require user explicit opt-in to include logs in snapshot; redact by default.

Next steps / owners:
- Prod design polish: Maya (design) + Jon (PM) -> prototype HTML wireframe (due 2025-11-24).
- Backend spike on serialization and storage: Noah + infra -> estimate due 2025-11-17.
- Accessibility checklist and QA plan: Priya -> initial pass 2025-11-30.

Notes / references:
- Linked: Confluence:Trace-UX-Playbacks-Design (detailed comps), JIRA INF-2147 (create snapshot), Slack thread #trace-ux (links to user quotes).
- Related features: timeline cursor zoom (see file: timeline-cursor-zoom-and-filter-interactions-wip) - ensure integration point.

Timestamped meeting notes: 2025-11-12 grooming session: agreed on MVP = capture/playback + simple share. Compare and storage policies deferred to next sprint.

Quick sketch pointers (for prototyping):
- Top: header with snapshot badge list (small pills) > center: waterfall (playback overlay in top-left) > bottom: pager for logs + metrics aligned.
- Colors: use existing trace palette but add "snapshot" accent (teal) for markers.

Action items (immediate):
- Create prototype Figma frames for: create modal, playback bar, isolated snapshot view, compare view. Owner: Maya.
- Blocker check: confirm RBAC model for share links with security team (Jon).

If you're reviewing: please comment inline with disagreements on flow or missing edge cases.
